title: 23-Hour Wagner Marathon Tests Endurance on a Hard Seat
seoTitle: 23-Hour Wagner Marathon on a Hard Seat
subtitle: Criticometer reports 23 hours of Wagner on a rigid seat amid a heat wave
excerpt: During a heat wave, a music critic endured 23 hours in Bayreuth’s hard seat while listening to Wagner’s Ring cycle, highlighting the physical toll of devotion.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
During the celebration of the 150th anniversary of the renowned Bayreuth Festival, a music critic decided to take on a test of endurance: staying locked in a venue known for its hard seats while watching a 23‑hour marathon of Wagner’s works.

The venue’s peculiarity – famous for its lack of padding on the chairs – turned the experience into a physical challenge. The heat wave sweeping the region amplified the sense of discomfort, forcing the critic to bear the weight of his own body on a seat described as a “hard rock”. The account details the effort required to keep the posture for almost an entire day, with the lower back and glutes being the main targets of fatigue.

The program included the complete cycle of “Der Ring des Nibelungen”, presented at an accelerated pace, along with other pieces that make up the traditional repertoire of the festival. Each work demanded full attention, while the critic tried to balance musical appreciation with the need to cope with physical discomfort. The contrast between Wagner’s sonic grandeur and the seat’s rigidity created a unique situation, which was described as “asking a lot of the glutes”.

At the end of the journey, the critic reflected on the level of endurance required of music lovers in venues that do not prioritize physical comfort. The experience reinforces the notion that artistic appreciation can involve bodily sacrifices, especially when the historic venue maintains its tradition of unpadded seats, even under adverse weather conditions.

With information from The Guardian.
